name: Azure Virtual Machines (Windows Server)

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go D/F-series + Windows licence (East US)

sizes.name: Standard_D4als_v7
sizes.note: Add $0.046/vCPU-h Windows licence from this mode: exact Windows East US PAYG total $0.345/h.

modes.note: Retail Prices API (eastus, Consumption) 2026-09-28. D-series: hour = Linux price and Windows = +$0.046/vCPU-h exactly (D4s_v5 0.192 -> 0.376). F-series v2: Windows prices 0.177/0.354/0.708 (Linux 0.0846/0.169/0.338), so hour here = Windows price - 0.046*vCPU to keep the Windows total exact. Azure bills full minutes only (6 min 45 s -> 6 min). 'Stopped' (not deallocated) still bills cores.

modes.label: B-series burstable + Windows licence (East US)

sizes.name: Standard_B4als_v2
sizes.note: Adjusted base so the existing +$0.004/vCPU-h field yields the exact Windows total $0.152/h; actual Linux meter is $0.133/h.

modes.note: B-series Windows surcharge is only +$0.004/vCPU-h (B2s 0.0416 -> 0.0496, B2ms 0.0832 -> 0.0912, B4ms 0.166 -> 0.182). Burstable CPU credits: sustained high CPU is throttled to baseline.

modes.label: Azure Spot VM (representative East US)
modes.note: Variable price observed in official API; no SLA; can be evicted with 30 seconds notice.

storage.billing_note: Managed disks are billed by provisioned tier, rounded up to the next offered disk size, and prorated hourly; Standard SSD also charges transactions up to a per-tier hourly cap. The linear $0.075/GiB-month card field is only exact at tier boundaries.

network.ipv4_billing_note: Standard static IPv4 is charged regardless of the attached VM state; each partial IP hour is a full billed hour. Static IP billing starts in the second hour after creation and ends only when the IP resource is deleted.

free.conditions: Free-account signup requires phone number, Microsoft or GitHub account, and non-prepaid credit/debit card; upgrade to pay-as-you-go within 30 days or after credit is used to continue. Credit cannot buy Spot VMs and cannot combine with Azure Hybrid Benefit.

caveats: Disk: Standard SSD E10 (128 GiB) = $9.60/month -> $0.075/GiB-month; Windows OS disks default to 127 GiB and are billed per provisioned tier even when deallocated. Premium SSD P10 = $19.71/month.
Snapshots/images: $0.05/GB-month on Standard LRS/ZRS based on used data; $0.12/GB-month when stored on Premium SSD. Incremental snapshots bill changed blocks.
Egress: first 100 GB/month free, then $0.087/GB (Microsoft network routing, first 10 TB); $0.08/GB with Internet routing preference.
Azure Hybrid Benefit (BYO licence) removes the Windows surcharge; reservations / savings plan / Spot not encoded.
Free account: $200 credit for 30 days (encoded as one_time_credit) and 750 h/month of B2ts/B2pts/B2ats v2 for 12 months (not encoded).

The modeled rates are Windows Server, but Azure also permits Windows 11 VMs: eligible Windows 11 Enterprise E3/E5 or Azure Virtual Desktop Access users can bring licenses for production; Student/Free Trial and eligible Visual Studio offers can deploy Windows 11 for dev/test.

Hibernation is real memory-preserving pause/resume, but only selected D/E v5 families up to 64 GiB and selected GPU families up to 112 GiB support it; F-series and B-series sizes modeled in the card do not. Hibernated VMs stop compute billing but retain OS/data disk and networking charges; OS disk must be large enough for RAM.

Reserved VM Instances (1y/3y) and savings plans discount compute only; the Windows licence stays pay-as-you-go ($0.184/h on D4s_v5). Example D4s_v5 East US: Linux RI $1,038/1y or $1,993/3y; Linux savings plan $0.1316736/h (1y), $0.0883584/h (3y). Not encoded.
Egress after the first 100 GB/month: $0.087/GB from North America/Europe (encoded), $0.12/GB from Asia/Australia/Middle East-Africa, $0.181/GB from South America (first 10 TB).

The general Azure Free page currently says B1s, B2pts v2, and B2ats v2, while the Windows VM pricing page says B2ts v2, B2pts v2, and B2ats v2. The Intel SKU is inconsistent across Microsoft pages and should not be normalized without account-level confirmation.

fleet.verification: Azure signup uses phone and non-prepaid card for identity verification.
fleet.notes: Regional total vCPU and VM-family vCPU quotas both apply, plus VM-count quotas. Applied values depend on subscription/region; no universal fresh-account numeric quota verified. Portal quota request may require review. GPU capacity is not guaranteed by approval.
fleet.quota_mechanics: Both Total Regional vCPU and VM-family vCPU quotas apply; allocated and deallocated VMs count. Spot has a separate pool. Quota increases use a support request, and approved quota does not guarantee capacity.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: The virtual machine has released the lease on the underlying hardware. If the machine is powered off it is shown as Stopped (Deallocated). If it has entered hibernation it is shown as Hibernated (Deallocated)
snapshot_auto.note: Stop/deallocate keeps the managed OS/data disks (persistent disk), and memory is only preserved if you explicitly hibernate (an API/portal action, not automatic on idle/stop). No idle auto-stop-with-snapshot. Azure Backup (scheduled daily/hourly policies, snapshot then vault copy) and scheduled restore-point collections are scheduled backups, not this.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: To recover by using a snapshot, create a managed disk from the snapshot. Then use the managed disk as the OS disk for a new VM or attach it as a data disk to an existing VM.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Managed-disk snapshots (full or incremental, portal/CLI/PowerShell/REST) of OS or data disks, running or stopped; disk only, no memory. New VMs can boot from them (also via VM restore points, which capture VM config plus all disks, and Azure Compute Gallery images). Memory state only via hibernation ('Azure stores the memory contents of the VM in the OS disk, then deallocates the VM'), which resumes the same VM and cannot be forked.

harness_api.quote: The Run Command feature uses the virtual machine (VM) agent to run PowerShell scripts within an Azure Windows VM.
harness_api.note: Only generic script execution (Run Command, Custom Script Extension); no first-party API to drive an agent harness inside the VM.

egress_allowlist.quote: A network security group contains security rules that allow or deny inbound network traffic to, or outbound network traffic from, several types of Azure resources.
egress_allowlist.note: NSG outbound rules = IP/CIDR/port/protocol/service-tag level (default AllowInternetOutBound can be overridden with deny rules), free. Domain level needs Azure Firewall (separate paid service, traffic routed via UDR): 'Application FQDN filtering rules: You can limit outbound HTTP/S traffic or Azure SQL traffic to a specified list of fully qualified domain names (FQDN) including wild cards.' Both enforced outside the guest.

egress_http_rules.quote: URL filtering extends Azure Firewall’s FQDN filtering capability to consider the entire URL, such as www.contoso.com/a/c instead of just www.contoso.com.
egress_http_rules.note: Azure Firewall Premium only (URL path filtering, HTTPS requires TLS inspection; also URL-based web categories and IDPS). No documented method- or header-based allow rules for egress. Standard SKU: 'URL filtering: Not supported (FQDN filtering only)'.

ingress_rules.quote: You can specify Any, an individual IP address, a CIDR block (for example, 10.0.0.0/24), a service tag, or an application security group.
ingress_rules.note: NSG inbound rules on NIC/subnet (default DenyAllInbound from Internet), public IP optional, plus Azure Firewall DNAT, Bastion, JIT VM access.

guest_firewall.quote: The guest system firewall profiles are set up to block all inbound connections, including the RDP traffic.
guest_firewall.note: Full Hyper-V VM with Administrator; Windows Defender Firewall inside the guest is configurable and takes effect (Microsoft troubleshooting docs cover it blocking RDP). Windows equivalent of nftables/iptables.

secret_proxy.quote: When it detects a change, the extension retrieves and installs the corresponding certificates.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets reach the VM: Key Vault (read by the VM via managed identity tokens from IMDS) and the Key Vault VM extension install certificates into the guest. No first-party proxy that injects credentials into outbound requests (Azure API Management/App Gateway are separate and not VM egress proxies).

volume_attach.quote: This article shows you how to attach a new managed data disk to a Windows virtual machine (VM) by using the Azure portal.
volume_attach.note: Managed data disks (Standard HDD/SSD, Premium SSD, Premium SSD v2, Ultra), hot-attachable; count limited by VM size.

volume_shared.quote: Azure shared disks is a feature for Azure managed disks that allows you to attach a managed disk to multiple virtual machines (VMs) simultaneously.
volume_shared.note: Shared managed disks (maxShares>1; Ultra, Premium SSD v2, Premium SSD, Standard SSD) are block-level read-write for all nodes but need a cluster manager (e.g. Windows Server Failover Cluster / SCSI PR) to coordinate writes. Simpler multi-VM read-write shared filesystem: Azure Files SMB shares mounted on Windows ('This article shows you how to mount an SMB Azure file share on Windows and Windows Server.').
